sources.citation: SIL International (Philippines). [1962-1966]. Addassen - Ba-y, Abra Wordlist (1962 Philippine Word List, 304 items, informant Julio Parinas; typed transcription). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 77088. Unpublished data set, CC BY-NC-SA.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose at all. Stress is transcribed with a raised tick before the stressed syllable on a subset of items, and it falls on both penults ('bagat, bo'sali, na'pit, na'ngisit) and final syllables (ɨ'min, dap'pog, bɨs'sog, bɨg'gi, baŋ'ka, bɨk'kag, kagab'bi) -- i.e. the raw data look like Ilokano/Isnag-type lexically variable penult-vs-final stress, but no rule is stated.

sources.note: First-hand survey of Northern Luzon speech varieties with wordlists and grammatical notes (Reid 1981: 'an excellent source for lexical and grammatical material from the Northern Philippine languages'); 'Adasen' as a language name in the pre-2005 literature most plausibly traces to McFarland 1977/1980. Whether an Adasen sample point is included, and whether accent is transcribed or described, is unverified.

sources.citation: New Tribes Mission (translators unnamed). Materials behind the Adasen New Testament 'Ya Baru nga Tulag' (1990): orthography statement / phonemic write-up / literacy primers for Adasen.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only sustained linguistic work ever done on Adasen (Ethnologue 17: 'NT: 1990'; find.bible lists the NT). NTM teams normally wrote an unpublished phonemic statement before fixing an orthography; if it exists it is the only place an explicit Adasen stress statement is likely to be found.

sources.citation: SIL Philippines, sociolinguistic survey of the Itneg/Tinguian varieties of Abra (c. 2004-2007; unpublished survey report underlying Ethnologue 15-17 'Comprehension of Isnag 74%', the Eastern/Western Addasen dialect split and the 2005 division of Itneg into six languages).
